analysis.title: US midterms: Blue wave ushers in gridlock
key_insights: Democrats are projected by AP and the major TV networks to retake both the House and the Senate, ending unified Republican control of Washington. Vote counting is still continuing.

The scale of the Democratic advance exceeded what markets had priced before election day. Equities and futures sold off sharply at first, then pressure eased. At publication Nasdaq futures were down about 0.8%, S&P 500 futures down about 0.6% and the Nikkei down 3%.
UBS says already fragile tech sentiment is likely amplifying the move alongside the election result.

UBS reads the result as a referendum on the incumbent, consistent with negative presidential approval and elevated oil prices before the vote. It cautions against reading it as a broad Democratic policy mandate.

UBS expects legislative friction, not sharp policy change. Trump keeps veto power, Senate rules and divided government constrain sweeping tax or spending bills, and the executive branch keeps broad authority over tariffs and foreign policy.

A Democratic Congress gains oversight of the administration, confirmation authority over appointments and nominations, and more influence over spending and debt-limit talks. It also gets a platform to test policy on Social Security, healthcare and AI regulation ahead of 2028.

After the results Trump said he will work with Democrats and does not want to veto everything. UBS thinks markets pricing 2028 outcomes now is premature and expects investors to refocus on fundamentals.

Debt talks are the clearest bond-market risk. The 2027 debt-ceiling negotiations could soften scheduled social-program cuts and raise defense spending, which could reverse an expected narrowing in deficits and increase Treasury supply. Brinkmanship could raise bond volatility.
UBS still expects inflation to moderate, the Fed to finish raising rates and Treasury yields to settle lower.

On AI, broad federal restrictions would face legislative and presidential constraints, and state and local rules matter more for data-center timing and location. State government composition, including the Texas result, may matter more for individual data-center projects than congressional control.

UBS raised its aggregate AI capex forecasts to USD 1.0tr in 2026 and USD 1.4tr in 2027. Global investors are weighting overinvestment, financing and monetization risks more heavily, and UBS says higher volatility could become the new normal.

Positioning: UBS does not see a case for an immediate strategic shift. It stays constructive on equities on earnings and AI investment, and advises reducing single-name concentration, rebalancing oversized tech exposure and tilting toward quality across the AI value chain. It suggests using politically driven weakness to rebalance or build exposure gradually.
UBS sees income and diversification value in high-quality short- to medium-term bonds and remains cautious on the longest maturities because of persistent deficits and heavy issuance.

sector_views.rationale: Near-term volatility is expected in tech and regulation-sensitive areas. UBS advises rebalancing oversized tech exposure and tilting toward quality AI value-chain companies, while AI demand remains strong.

sector_views.sector: Fixed income (short- to medium-term high-quality bonds)
sector_views.rationale: Current yields offer attractive income and diversification. UBS is cautious on the longest maturities because of persistent deficits and heavy issuance.

earnings_insights: UBS cites strong earnings, together with AI investment, as support for its constructive equity view. The report gives no specific EPS or revenue figures.

trade_ideas.description: Rebalance or gradually build equity exposure on politically driven weakness, tilting within technology toward quality companies across the AI value chain
trade_ideas.rationale: Strong earnings and AI investment support the constructive equity view, and the election result does not change the medium-term fundamental outlook enough to justify a strategic shift.
trade_ideas.risk: Politically driven volatility in tech and regulation-sensitive areas, and AI overinvestment, financing and monetization concerns.

trade_ideas.description: Add exposure to high-quality short- to medium-term bonds for income and diversification, staying cautious on the longest maturities
trade_ideas.rationale: Current yields offer attractive income, though persistent deficits and heavy issuance underpin caution on the longest maturities.
trade_ideas.risk: 2027 debt-ceiling talks could reverse the expected narrowing in deficits and increase Treasury supply.

vol_and_positioning: UBS says the more definitive Democratic outcome could drive near-term volatility, particularly in tech and areas sensitive to regulatory scrutiny.
Potential debt-ceiling brinkmanship in 2027 could heighten bond-market volatility.
UBS says higher volatility could become the new normal for AI-related equities, favoring financially strong platforms and infrastructure providers and diversified exposure across the AI value chain.
Positioning advice: reduce single-name concentration and rebalance oversized tech exposure.

Trump retains veto power and broad executive authority over tariffs and foreign policy.
2027 debt-ceiling negotiations could shift spending toward defense and soften scheduled social-program cuts.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong earnings and AI investment support a constructive equity view, and gridlock should limit sharp policy changes. Trump says he will work with Democrats and does not want to veto everything.
tension_points.bear_case: The Democratic win was larger than priced, tech sentiment is fragile, and greater oversight and regulatory scrutiny could drive near-term volatility in tech.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Policy changes that materially alter the fundamental outlook would prompt UBS to adjust portfolios.

tension_points.bull_case: Inflation moderates, the Fed finishes raising rates and Treasury yields settle lower.
tension_points.bear_case: 2027 debt-ceiling talks could soften social-program cuts and raise defense spending, reversing the expected narrowing in deficits and increasing Treasury supply.

theme_stances.key_argument: Expect legislative friction rather than a reversal of the administration's agenda, so the result does not change the medium-term outlook enough to justify a strategic shift.
theme_stances.evidence: Expect sand in the legislative gears, not sharp policy changes.

theme_stances.key_argument: Greater congressional oversight will not necessarily derail the AI investment cycle, and state and local rules matter more.
